description: Fast-lane role routing: which team role takes part in a task, and when. A rule matches a task of one of its kinds when any trigger hits: the task size, a file the task names or changes (shell globs, * crosses /), or a keyword in its title or text (whole word, plural allowed). mode require blocks open-pr until the role's verdict is recorded; suggest never blocks; off drops a packaged rule. pre_check_triggers names, per task size, the trigger kinds (size, path, keyword) that may route a rule at that size; a size with none routes no role. spawn_modes are the modes whose roles start and approve list in spawn, the roles the flow spawns on its own; a role of another mode spawns only when the owner asks. model_class, when a rule names one, is the purpose class its pre-check spawn runs on. step pre_check is a bounded review of the task and its plan before writing; author means the role writes the change. A project replaces a rule of the same role, or adds one, in role_routing of workspace/config.json with the same rules shape; pre_check_triggers and spawn_modes there replace the packaged ones.

rules.ask: Check the task and its plan against the architecture records and the solution design: data model and schema changes, module and service boundaries, public interfaces and contracts, cross-component dependencies. Return go, or changes with a reason for each; a minor finding becomes an issue instead of a change.
Check the task against the solution landscape and its decision log: product choice, integration and runtime placement. Return go, or changes with a reason for each.
Check the acceptance criteria against the approved analysis: business rules, process steps and edge cases. Return go, or changes with a reason for each.
Check that each acceptance criterion has a named test that proves it, and name the live group the change can affect. Return go, or changes with a reason for each.
